cause.what_happened: OPNW (formerly VerifyMe) is in its third week after a reverse merger closed 2026-09-30. It fell 17.6% by 15:05 ET (8.5% overnight gap, 9.9% intraday) on 0.58x its merger-inflated 20-day dollar volume, with no 8-K, press release or news dated 10-13 found. The fall continues a 5-day run-up of -32.9%, read as post-merger float supply: the 10% lock-up tranche released 9-30 (about 76% of shares are restricted), legacy VerifyMe holders (about 1.43M shares), a $199k Form 144 sale by a departing director on 10-06, and Maxim's 361k advisor shares.

findings.finding: The 9-30 merger 8-K says the co-transfer-agent period (West Coast Stock Transfer alongside Vinyl Equity) is expected to end around 2026-10-13. Consolidating the register after the 10% lock-up release eases deposit and sale of the freely tradeable legacy shares in the days around the window.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The company dated it in the 8-K to about 2026-10-13, so any easing of delivery of released or legacy shares applies to the 10-14 session.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line. Since the merger closed, the name has fallen on 10-01 (-25.9%), 10-08 (-12.9%), 10-09 (-15.3%) and today, with no news on the last three. That fits continuing float supply but is not specific to the transfer agent.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and inferential. The price holds the steady post-merger selling but not any discrete increase in deliverable shares. If the transfer-agent change freed nothing new, tomorrow looks like the base rate. If it did, more low-volume grinding lower would follow.
